Question
Let X and Y be sets of the same universe with |Y| < |X|. Any observation map h:X→Y takes the same value on two distinct inputs.

Definitions: |X| and |Y| denote set cardinalities.; h:X→Y is a total function labelled an observation map; no additional observation structure is defined.
Hypotheses: X and Y are sets in the same universe.; |Y|<|X|.
Quantifiers: For every same-universe pair X,Y satisfying |Y|<|X|, for every total function h:X→Y, there exist x0,x1 in X. The pair may depend on h. No finiteness or nonemptiness assumption is imposed; if no such function exists, the quantification over h is vacuous.
Conclusion: x0≠x1 and h(x0)=h(x1), equivalently h is not injective under the standard classical interpretation.

Question
Let finite sets A,B,C satisfy |C|≤|B|<|A|. For maps f:A→B and g:B→C, distinct a,a′ satisfy g(f(a))=g(f(a′)).

Definitions: |X| is the number of elements of a finite set X.; The composition g∘f sends a∈A to g(f(a))∈C.
Hypotheses: A,B,C are finite sets.; |C|≤|B|.; |B|<|A|.; f:A→B is a total function.; g:B→C is a total function.
Quantifiers: For every finite A,B,C satisfying the cardinality inequalities, for every f:A→B and every g:B→C, there exist a,a′∈A. The pair may depend on the maps. No nonemptiness assumption is added; nonexistent function choices give vacuous cases.
Conclusion: There exist a,a′∈A such that a≠a′ and g(f(a))=g(f(a′)).

Question
Let nonempty finite sets X,Y satisfy |Y|≤|X|. Every h:X→Y takes equal values at two distinct inputs.

Definitions: X and Y are sets; |X| and |Y| denote their finite cardinalities.; h:X→Y is a total function.; A collision consists of x,x' in X with x≠x' and h(x)=h(x').
Hypotheses: X is finite and nonempty.; Y is finite and nonempty.; |Y|≤|X|, including equality.
Quantifiers: For every pair X,Y satisfying the hypotheses, for every total function h:X→Y, there exist x,x' in X. The pair may depend on X,Y,h. Singleton sets and equal cardinalities are included.
Conclusion: There exist x,x' in X such that x≠x' and h(x)=h(x').

Question
In a commutative ring R let p²=p+1, q²=q+1, p+q=1 and pq=−1; let m be a nonnegative integer. For u_j=a p^j+b q^j, u_(m+1)²−u_(m+1)u_m−u_m²=−5ab(−1)^m.

Definitions: u_j=a*p^j+b*q^j for every nonnegative integer j; powers are natural powers.
Hypotheses: R is a commutative ring, with the identity implicitly used by the constants 1 and -1.; a,b,p,q are elements of R; a and b have this intended implicit domain.; p^2=p+1.; q^2=q+1.; p+q=1.; p*q=-1.
Quantifiers: For every commutative ring R under the stated identity convention, every p,q in R satisfying the four equations, every a,b in R, and every m in the nonnegative integers, with u_j defined for all nonnegative integers j.
Conclusion: u_(m+1)^2-u_(m+1)*u_m-u_m^2=-5*a*b*(-1)^m, with all constants and operations interpreted in R.

Question
For real symmetric idempotent N×N matrices P_1,…,P_n, let M be their mean and S the average of all n! ordered products. For every n≥1,N, M^n−S is positive semidefinite.

Definitions: P_i are real orthogonal projections: P_i^T=P_i and P_i^2=P_i.; M=(1/n) sum_{i=1}^n P_i.; S=(1/n!) sum_{sigma in Sym(n)} P_sigma(1)...P_sigma(n), counting label permutations even when matrices repeat.; M^n-S is positive semidefinite iff x^T(M^n-S)x>=0 for every x in R^N.
Hypotheses: n is an integer with n>=1.; N is a finite matrix dimension.; Every P_i is a real N-by-N symmetric idempotent matrix.
Quantifiers: For every integer n>=1 and every finite matrix dimension N, for every tuple (P_1,...,P_n) satisfying the hypotheses, the conclusion holds. No commutativity, distinctness, rank restriction, or relation between n and N is assumed. N=0 is vacuous if zero-dimensional matrices are allowed.
Conclusion: S<=M^n in Loewner order, equivalently M^n-S is positive semidefinite.

Question
For any three orthogonal projections E,F,G on R³, ((E+F+G)/3)^3−(EFG+EGF+FEG+FGE+GEF+GFE)/6 is positive semidefinite.

Definitions: An orthogonal projection on Euclidean R^3 is a real 3x3 matrix P with P^T=P and P^2=P.; A symmetric matrix D is positive semidefinite when x^T D x>=0 for every x in R^3.; Products and powers are ordinary matrix multiplication; the six displayed products average all permutations of the three labeled factors.
Hypotheses: E,F,G are orthogonal projections on R^3.; There are no rank, distinctness, commutativity, mutual-orthogonality or sum-to-identity restrictions.
Quantifiers: For every E,F,G in M_3(R) satisfying the projection equations, the conclusion holds for every x in R^3. Include ranks 0 through 3, zero and identity projections, and repeated projections.
Conclusion: ((E+F+G)/3)^3-(EFG+EGF+FEG+FGE+GEF+GFE)/6 is positive semidefinite.

Question
For real symmetric idempotent N×N matrices P_1,…,P_n, let M be their mean and S the average of all n! ordered products. Restrict to n=2. The cited n=3 counterexample proves that M²−S fails to be positive semidefinite for some P_1,P_2.

Definitions: M=(1/n) sum_{i=1}^n P_i.; S=(1/n!) sum_{sigma in Sym(n)} P_{sigma(1)}...P_{sigma(n)}, counting labeled permutations.; At n=2, M=(P_1+P_2)/2 and S=(P_1P_2+P_2P_1)/2.; For symmetric D, D is PSD iff x^T D x>=0 for every x in R^N.
Hypotheses: n=2.; P_1,P_2 are real N-by-N matrices.; P_i^T=P_i and P_i^2=P_i for i=1,2; no commutation, rank, invertibility or distinctness assumption.
Quantifiers: For the implicit finite dimension N, existence of P_1,P_2 satisfying the hypotheses and a nonzero x in R^N with x^T(M^2-S)x<0. N is not explicitly quantified: distinguish fixed-N and dimension-existential readings. Conventionally N>=1; N=0, if allowed, has no such x.
Conclusion: M^2-S is not PSD for some admissible pair. C1 also asserts that an unidentified cited n=3 counterexample establishes this n=2 conclusion.

Definitions: Sample space: s=(X,R), X:A->Y, R_a:{b in A:b!=a}->Y.; Listing g_s(a,b)=X(a) if b=a, otherwise R_a(b).; Weight w(s)=(product_b q(b,X(b)))(product_a product_{b!=a} q(b,R_a(b))).; Twisted diagonal d_s(b)=f(g_s(b,b)).; C(s)=#{a in A: for every b in A, g_s(a,b)=d_s(b)}.; T_k=sum_{s:C(s)>=k} w(s); B_k=sum_s binom(C(s),k)w(s).
Hypotheses: A and Y are finite, possibly empty.; q:A×Y->R and q(a,y)>=0 for every a,y.; f:Y->Y is arbitrary.
Quantifiers: For every finite A,Y, every q and f of the stated types with q nonnegative everywhere, and every k in N={0,1,...}. Sums range over all source samples.
Conclusion: T_k<=B_k for every natural k, including k=0, k>|A|, and empty sample spaces, with standard binomial and empty-index conventions.
